scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

prediction.raw: I can provide you with a neutral analysis of the situation. In this scenario, it seems like you're feeling disappointed and hurt that your husband prioritized watching video game streams over spending time with you and the kids. You had asked him to turn off the stream and spend time with you, but he declined, citing that it's his free time and he shouldn't have to stop doing something he enjoys just because you want him to. However, you also mention that he spent a significant amount of money on in-app purchases for the same game last year, which you're not okay with. This suggests that you have concerns about his spending habits and the impact it has on your family. From a neutral perspective, it's not necessarily about being an "asshole" for having expectations or being upset. It's about communication and compromise in a relationship. It sounds like you're feeling neglected and unimportant in this situation, and that's a valid feeling. It might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with your husband about your feelings and concerns. You could express how you feel when he prioritizes his gaming over spending time with you and the kids, and also discuss your concerns about his spending habits. It's possible that he's not aware of the impact his actions have on you, and talking it through might help you find a compromise that works for both of you. As for whether your expectations are "realistic," it's not necessarily about what's "realistic" but about what's fair and respectful in your relationship. You have a right to feel seen and prioritized in your relationship, and it's okay to express those feelings and needs to your partner. So, I'd say you're not an asshole for feeling upset and having expectations. You're simply expressing your needs and feelings, and it's up to your husband to listen and respond in a way that respects and prioritizes your relationship.
